items.followUp: Explain the formation of an ionic bond in magnesium oxide (MgO).

rubric.why: The definition must identify electron transfer and the resulting oppositely charged ions.
rubric.description: Defines ionic bond by electron transfer and formation of oppositely charged ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for electron transfer and 1 mark for formation of oppositely charged ions.

rubric.why: Sodium forms a positive ion by losing an electron.
rubric.description: Explains formation of the sodium ion in the example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that sodium loses an electron to form Na+.

rubric.why: Chlorine forms a negative ion by gaining an electron.
rubric.description: Explains formation of the chloride ion in the example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chlorine gains an electron to form Cl−.

rubric.why: The opposite charges attract and form the ionic compound.
rubric.description: Identifies the attraction holding the ions together in sodium chloride.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electrostatic attraction between Na+ and Cl− forms NaCl.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by the transfer of electrons from one atom to another.
For example, a sodium atom loses one electron to form a sodium ion: Na → Na+ + e−.
A chlorine atom gains this electron to form a chloride ion: Cl + e− → Cl−.
The oppositely charged Na+ and Cl− ions attract each other and form sodium chloride (NaCl).

items.followUp: Define rusting and explain how painting prevents it.

rubric.why: The definition should describe the gradual deterioration of a metal through reaction with its surroundings.
rubric.description: Defines corrosion as the gradual destruction or deterioration of a metal by its environment.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for the idea of gradual metal deterioration caused by reaction with the environment.

rubric.why: The method involves covering iron with a layer of zinc.
rubric.description: Identifies zinc coating (galvanizing) of iron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that iron is coated with zinc.

rubric.why: A zinc coating shields iron from the substances needed for corrosion.
rubric.description: Explains that the coating blocks air and moisture from reaching the iron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the barrier against air and moisture.

rubric.why: Zinc is more reactive and corrodes preferentially, protecting iron even if the coating is damaged.
rubric.description: Explains zinc's sacrificial protection of iron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that zinc corrodes or oxidizes preferentially and protects the iron.

modelAnswer: Corrosion is the gradual destruction or deterioration of a metal due to its reaction with substances in the environment.
Iron can be protected by coating it with zinc; this process is called galvanizing.
The zinc layer prevents air and moisture from reaching the iron.
Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it corrodes preferentially and protects the iron, even if the coating is scratched.

items.followUp: Define solubility and state three factors that affect it.

rubric.why: Solubility specifies how much solute dissolves to make a saturated solution under stated conditions.
rubric.description: Defines solubility as the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a specified temperature to form a saturated solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the maximum-solute/saturated-solution definition.

rubric.why: The identities of the solute and solvent affect whether and how much solute dissolves.
rubric.description: Names the nature of the solute and/or solvent as a factor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the nature of the solute or solvent.

rubric.why: Solubility depends on temperature.
rubric.description: Names temperature as a factor affecting solubility.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying temperature.

rubric.why: Pressure affects the solubility of gases in liquids.
rubric.description: Names pressure as a factor affecting solubility, particularly for gases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying pressure.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a specified temperature to form a saturated solution.
Three factors that affect solubility are the nature of the solute and solvent, temperature, and pressure (especially for gases).

items.followUp: Define a compound and state how it is represented.

rubric.why: An element consists of only one kind of atom and cannot be broken down chemically into simpler substances.
rubric.description: Defines an element as a pure substance made of one kind of atom and not decomposable by chemical means.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the one-kind-of-atom definition or equivalent.

rubric.why: Elements are represented by chemical symbols.
rubric.description: States that an element is represented by a chemical symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying chemical symbols as the representation.

modelAnswer: An element is a pure substance made up of only one kind of atom and cannot be decomposed into simpler substances by chemical means.
An element is represented by a chemical symbol, such as H for hydrogen or O for oxygen.

items.followUp: An atom has mass number A = 35 and atomic number Z = 17. Find its number of protons and neutrons.

rubric.why: The atomic number equals the number of protons.
rubric.description: Determines the number of protons from Z.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the atom has 92 protons.

rubric.why: Neutrons equal mass number minus atomic number: A − Z.
rubric.description: Calculates the number of neutrons using A − Z.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the subtraction or the correct result of 146 neutrons.

modelAnswer: Given: A = 238 and Z = 92.
Number of protons = Z = 92.
Number of neutrons = A − Z = 238 − 92 = 146.
Therefore, the atom has 92 protons and 146 neutrons.

items.followUp: Define a diatomic molecule and give one example.

rubric.why: Triatomic means that a molecule contains three atoms.
rubric.description: Defines a triatomic molecule by its number of atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it contains three atoms.

rubric.why: A valid example must be a molecule containing three atoms.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example, such as H₂O, O₃, or CO₂.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

modelAnswer: A triatomic molecule is a molecule that contains three atoms.
For example, a water molecule (H₂O) contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

items.followUp: Define ionization energy and state its trend down a group.

rubric.why: Ionization energy is the energy needed to remove an electron from an atom.
rubric.description: Defines ionization energy as the energy required to remove an electron from an atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the energy-to-remove-an-electron definition.

rubric.why: Across a period, ionization energy generally increases from left to right.
rubric.description: States the trend of ionization energy across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the increasing left-to-right trend.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
Across a period, ionization energy generally increases from left to right.

items.followUp: Describe how atomic radius changes down a group and give the reason.

rubric.why: Atomic radius becomes smaller across a period from left to right.
rubric.description: States the direction of the atomic-radius trend across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atomic radius decreases from left to right.

rubric.why: Increasing nuclear charge attracts the electrons more strongly without adding a new electron shell.
rubric.description: Gives the reason for the decrease in atomic radius across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking increasing nuclear charge to a stronger pull on the electrons or a smaller radius.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius decreases from left to right across a period.
The nuclear charge increases while electrons are added to the same shell, so the stronger attraction pulls the electrons closer to the nucleus.
